title: Nvidia just printed $115.8 billion in revenue. So why is the stockstill stuck in a fight over who runs the company?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[NVDA\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/NVDA/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/NVDA/)) reported fiscal Q3 revenue  
of $115.84 billion, up 103% year over year and ahead of both company  
guidance and consensus. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.68, versus about  
$2.47 expected.  
  
This write-up is from last night's report (Nov 17), so check the  
latest price before you post. Mid-session today the stock was around  
$151, and the leadership transition is still part of the debate.  
  
The Q3 recap, including the beat and the leadership backdrop:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/nvidia-nvda-delivers-solid-fiscal-q3-results-amid-leadership-transition-39994/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/nvidia-nvda-delivers-solid-fiscal-q3-results-amid-leadership-transition-39994/)  
  
Does a quarter like this settle the argument, or does the CEO fight  
still matter more than the numbers?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from last night's write-up, not a live quote.
